analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (date bump and a new Gemma 4 pipeline-lane paragraph, head lines 1085-1094) and docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump, Gemma pipeline lanes section, Gemma routed-expert prior, shared routed-expert dispatch text). It changes no executable code, wire protocol, attestation, authorization, encryption or key handling, so it adds no new attack surface and weakens no mitigation.

Threat-model checks:
- TB-002, TB-003 and TB-007 are unaffected. The docs describe a default cluster lane width of 4 for serial-prefill Gemma 4 pipelines (`DistributedInstalledPlan.gemma4PipelineBatchLanes`). Each lane is admitted against live memory (`QwenResidentRuntime.reserveLane`), is refused retryably, and retires alone on cancel. No decrypt/re-encrypt hop or consumer-key handling is described as changing.
- T-041 (prefix cache and timing oracle): the docs mention Gemma paged prefix restoration only by reference. They state no change to cache scoping, TTL or HMAC lookup keys, so the accepted SEC-035 posture is unchanged.
- The doc claims the shared routed-expert call keeps each token's bytes identical to its one-token call and leaves the arithmetic receipt and cache identities unchanged. That is a correctness/qualification claim, not a security control. I could not verify it from the supplied evidence.
- Multi-lane concurrency raises the cross-request co-residency of decrypted prompts in one process (A-001). The threat model already treats the provider as holding plaintext during inference (T-014, T-028), so this is not a new class of exposure.

Open integration questions for the next pass: whether the corresponding code change, which is not in this batch, preserves per-lane isolation (KV, cancellation, cache salt) in `CBv2StageKVHost` and `QwenResidentRuntime`; and whether the default width of 4 bypasses admission limits. The docs assert neither, and I cannot check either from this batch. The `inference.md` patch excerpt is truncated, though the head text covers the changed ranges that were shown.
